name: FLARE (Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation) - Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
venue: EMNLP 2023 (Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pages 7969-7992); preprint arXiv:2305.06983 (v1 11 May 2023, v2 22 Oct 2023).
authors_affiliation: Zhengbao Jiang, Frank F. Xu, Luyu Gao, Zhiqing Sun, Yiming Yang, Jamie Callan, Graham Neubig (Language Technologies Institute, Carnegie Mellon University); Qian Liu (Sea AI Lab); Jane Dwivedi-Yu (FAIR, Meta). First four authors are equal-contribution.
code_url: https://github.com/jzbjyb/FLARE (official author implementation, MIT license, Python; ~667 stars, 60 forks; uses Elasticsearch/BM25 over the DPR Wikipedia dump and Bing search; includes code + datasets + few-shot configs).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper author repo; last pushed 2023-11-20; not a continuously-updated leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: Long-form, knowledge-intensive text generation with LLMs: multihop QA, commonsense reasoning, long-form QA, and open-domain summarization. Framed as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the course of long-text generation rather than agentic tool-use.
problem_setting: Offline, single-model, inference-time (test-time) setting with a frozen black-box LLM (GPT-3.5 text-davinci-003 accessed via API; gpt-3.5-turbo used to generate explicit questions). No training/fine-tuning of the LM or retriever; off-the-shelf retrievers (BM25 over a Wikipedia dump, or the Bing search engine for open-web tasks). Few-shot in-context learning with task-specific exemplars. Single agent, no multi-agent interaction. The core problem is deciding WHEN and WHAT to retrieve during long-form generation, so that retrieval is interleaved with generation. FLARE generalizes single-time retrieve-and-generate to active retrieval triggered by the LM's own token-level confidence, querying with an anticipated (forward-looking) next sentence.
what_is_retrieved: Documents / passages (Wikipedia passages via BM25, or open-web pages via Bing search) that provide factual knowledge to ground the next sentence being generated. Not demonstrations, tools, cases, or agent experiences.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed Wikipedia dump (psgs_w100 from Karpukhin et al. 2020, indexed with BM25/Elasticsearch) for Wikipedia-grounded tasks, and the live open web via the Bing search engine for the open-domain summarization (WikiAsp) task. There is no growing/episodic agent memory; the knowledge store is external and not written to by the system.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k document ranking per retrieval call, with k set per dataset (top-2 for 2WikiMultihopQA, top-3 for StrategyQA and ASQA, top-5 for WikiAsp). The objective is similarity-style top-k document retrieval to ground each sentence, not recovery of a minimal complete set nor a precision-driven variable-size set. (For the explicit-question variant, documents retrieved by multiple generated questions are interleaved into a single ranking list.)
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve] only. FLARE retrieves documents; there is no case Reuse/Revise/Retain in the CBR sense (no case library, no case adaptation, no retention of solved cases). Not a CBR method.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: FLARE does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is a retrieval-augmented generation method.
retrieval_unit: Document / passage (a retrieved document or web page snippet). The decision/iteration unit of generation is the sentence (a temporary next sentence), but the retrieved unit itself is a document/passage.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced for Wikipedia tasks (BM25/Elasticsearch index over the fixed DPR Wikipedia dump); live web index for WikiAsp (Bing search engine, with several Wikipedia-related domains excluded to avoid leakage). No online/test-time growth of the store driven by the agent.
index_structure_topology: Flat inverted/lexical index: BM25 over Elasticsearch for Wikipedia passages, and the Bing web-search backend for open-web retrieval. No graph, hierarchy, or cluster topology.
retriever_type: Off-the-shelf sparse/lexical retriever (BM25, Robertson & Zaragoza 2009) over Wikipedia, and the Bing search engine (a black-box web search API) for open-web tasks. No dense or learned retriever; the retriever is fixed and not trained.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): the retriever (BM25 / Bing) is not trained or fine-tuned. FLARE focuses on the integration of retrieval and generation, deliberately using off-the-shelf retrievers; the novelty is in query construction and trigger timing rather than in learning a retriever. The only learned signal is the LM's own token probabilities/calibration used as a trigger, not a retriever-training objective.
query_construction: Forward-looking, generation-conditioned query. At each step the LM first generates a temporary next sentence s_hat_t = LM([x, y_<t]) WITHOUT retrieval; this anticipated sentence becomes the basis of the query. Two query-formulation methods over s_hat_t: (1) implicit -- mask out low-confidence tokens (probability below threshold beta) to remove distractions; (2) explicit -- prompt gpt-3.5-turbo to generate targeted questions for each low-confidence span. FLARE-instruct alternatively prompts the LM to emit [Search(query)] queries via retrieval-encouraging instructions. The initial query (t=1) is the raw user input x.
query_granularity: Step/sentence-level: a new query is constructed at each generation step (per sentence) from the anticipated next sentence, interleaving retrieval and generation throughout long-form output. Not a single task-level query at t=0 (except the initial bootstrap query which is the user input).
when_to_retrieve: Active (uncertainty/confidence-triggered) and iterative: retrieval is triggered during generation only when the anticipated next sentence contains a low-probability (low-confidence) token; otherwise the sentence is accepted without retrieval. This interleaves retrieval and generation adaptively across the course of long-text generation.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Token-level confidence (LM probability). Retrieval is triggered if ANY token of the anticipated next sentence s_hat_t has a generation probability below a threshold theta in [0,1] (theta=0 never retrieves, theta=1 retrieves every sentence). Motivated by the observation that large LMs are well-calibrated and low probability indicates lack of knowledge (Kadavath et al. 2022). FLARE-instruct uses an alternative agent-initiated trigger: the LM emits a [Search(query)] token sequence.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Retrieved documents are linearized in their retriever ranking order. For the explicit-question variant, documents from multiple generated questions are interleaved into a single ranking list, but no learned/cross-encoder reranker is applied.
retrieved_context_refinement: Query-side refinement rather than document-side: low-confidence tokens are masked out of the query (implicit) or converted into targeted questions (explicit) to improve retrieval accuracy and remove distractions. Retrieved documents themselves are used with light processing (linearized by rank, prepended to the input; only current-step documents are kept and previous retrieved documents are discarded to fit the context limit). No document distillation, compression, or relevance filtering of returned documents.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; documents are raw retrieved passages/web results, not engineered tool descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A / No: retrieved documents are linearized and prepended directly; there is no lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index/protocol). Retrieval uses a static BM25 Wikipedia index and the live Bing web-search API; no MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling tool integration.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved documents D_qt are linearized by rank and prepended before the user input x and previous generation y_<t, then the LM regenerates the next sentence s_t = LM([D_qt, x, y_<t]). Only the current step's documents are used (previously retrieved documents are discarded) to avoid exceeding the input length limit. No fine-tuning; pure in-context conditioning.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-generate inside a generation loop (no explicit planner, MCTS, or tree search). Generation proceeds sentence by sentence; at each step the LM looks forward (generates a temporary sentence), conditionally retrieves, then regenerates, until the end of the long-form answer. For multihop QA / commonsense it operates over chain-of-thought generation, so retrieval is woven into the CoT reasoning chain.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-sentence: retrieval is interleaved at the granularity of each generated sentence (the iteration unit), which for CoT tasks corresponds to per-CoT-step. The trigger decision is informed at the token level (any low-probability token in the sentence), but the interleaving/regeneration granularity is the sentence.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no case adaptation). The closest analog is regeneration of the next sentence conditioned on newly retrieved documents when low confidence is detected.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved document/passage text, linearized by rank (format: 'Search results: [1] Document 1 [2] Document 2 ... The user input x') and prepended to the prompt. No distilled strategy, workflow, or latent representation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/passage (un-distilled factual text from Wikipedia or the web). Not a distilled strategy, guideline, workflow, skill, or demonstration.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Query-side noise reduction: low-confidence tokens (likely erroneous/hallucinated) are masked out of the query (implicit) or replaced by targeted questions (explicit) so they do not distract the retriever; ablations confirm masking low-probability tokens (beta=0.4) beats using the full sentence (beta=0). Confidence-gated retrieval also avoids unnecessary retrieval when the LM is confident, since the ablation shows over-retrieval can introduce noise and hurt performance (e.g., StrategyQA drops past ~50% retrieval). No retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, or reason-in-documents distillation of returned passages.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/graph/latent memory; the external Wikipedia/web corpus is a static knowledge source, not an agent memory).
write_back: False: FLARE does not store new experiences, cases, or skills into any memory; it only reads from a fixed external corpus / web.
online_growth: No: the retrievable store (Wikipedia BM25 index / Bing web) does not grow as a function of the system's own generation; it is a fixed/external knowledge source.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back; no memory is maintained or updated).
failure_experience_usage: N/A / none: no storage or retrieval of failed experiences. The only use of 'failure-like' signal is at query time -- low-confidence (likely-wrong) tokens trigger retrieval and are masked from the query -- but nothing is stored.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate; append-only-none).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval/triggering is a fixed, hand-set rule (token-probability threshold theta plus off-the-shelf BM25/Bing), not an RL- or value-trained policy. Selection is threshold-gated top-k, not a learned MDP policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model, single private retrieval pipeline; no memory/experience shared across agents or frameworks.
benchmarks: 2WikiMultihopQA (multihop QA, 500 examples), StrategyQA (commonsense yes/no QA, 229 examples), ASQA and ASQA-hint (long-form/ambiguous QA, 500 examples), WikiAsp (open-domain aspect-based summarization, 500 examples). FLARE was also tried on Wizard of Wikipedia and ELI5 (reported in Limitations as showing no significant gains).
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (2WikiMultihopQA), commonsense QA (StrategyQA), long-form QA (ASQA), and open-domain summarization (WikiAsp). Knowledge-intensive long-form generation family; not in the standard web/embodied/tool/code/memory-agent benchmark families.
baselines: No retrieval (parametric LM only); Single-time retrieval (retrieve once on the input, retrieve-and-generate, a la REPLUG/IC-RALM style); and three multi-time retrieval categories reimplemented in the same framework: Previous-window (retrieve every l=16 tokens using the last window as query; representing RETRO/IC-RALM/KNN-LM), Previous-sentence (retrieve every sentence using the previous sentence; representing IRCoT, Trivedi et al. 2022), and Question decomposition (manually annotated sub-question exemplars; representing self-ask, Press et al. 2022). FLARE has two variants compared: FLARE-instruct (retrieval-instruction prompting, inspired by Toolformer) and FLARE-direct (confidence-based forward-looking, the main method).
key_metrics: 2WikiMultihopQA: Exact Match (EM, primary), token-level F1, Precision, Recall. StrategyQA: EM. ASQA / ASQA-hint: EM (str-EM, primary), Disambig-F1 (D-F1), ROUGE-L (R-L), and DR (Disambig-ROUGE composite). WikiAsp: UniEval (factual consistency, primary), named entity-based F1 (E-F1), ROUGE-L.
headline_result: On 2WikiMultihopQA, FLARE-direct achieves EM 51.0 / F1 59.7 / Prec. 59.1 / Rec. 62.6 with GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003), substantially beating no-retrieval (EM 28.2), single-time retrieval (EM 39.4), and the strongest multi-time baseline question-decomposition (EM 47.8). Across all 4 tasks/datasets FLARE achieves superior or competitive performance over single-time and multi-time retrieval baselines (e.g., StrategyQA EM 77.3 vs 72.9 no-retrieval; WikiAsp UniEval 37.2 vs 36.0 single-time).
ablations: 1) Forward-looking (next-sentence) vs past (previous-sentence) query (Table 3): retrieving with the NEXT sentence clearly beats the previous sentence (2WikiMultihopQA EM 48.8 vs 39.0; ASQA-hint EM 45.9 vs 42.5), confirming forward-looking queries reflect future intent. 2) Active-retrieval threshold theta (Figure 5): varying the % of sentences with retrieval -- on 2WikiMultihopQA performance plateaus past ~60% retrieval (confident-step retrieval is unnecessary); on StrategyQA performance DROPS past ~50% (over-retrieval injects noise); triggering retrieval for 40-80% of sentences works well. 3) Previous-window query length (Table 4): 16-32 tokens best (EM 43.2-43.6), 'All' tokens worst (EM 39.0). 4) Masking threshold beta (Table 5): beta=0.4 best (EM 51.0) vs beta=0 full sentence (EM 48.8), confirming low-confidence tokens distract the retriever. 5) Implicit vs explicit query formulation (Table 6): roughly comparable performance on ASQA-hint and WikiAsp. FLARE-direct strongly outperforms FLARE-instruct, indicating teaching the LM to emit search queries via generic retrieval instructions is hard.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end downstream generation metrics (EM/F1/UniEval/ROUGE/Disambig-F1) are reported. No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) for the retriever.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final answer/summary quality: EM, F1, UniEval, ROUGE). Process aspects are studied indirectly via the active-retrieval ablation (proportion of steps with retrieval vs performance) and the next-vs-previous-sentence comparison, but there is no scored reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency discussed qualitatively: FLARE triggers retrieval for ~30-60% of sentences on average (vs KNN-LM every token, RETRO/IC-RALM every 4-32 tokens, IRCoT every sentence), so it retrieves less than fixed-schedule multi-time baselines. However, the authors note in Limitations that interleaving generation and retrieval with a naive (caching-free) implementation increases overhead: the LM is activated multiple times (once per retrieval) and previous activations must be recomputed after each retrieval; experiments are 'relatively expensive' due to repeated OpenAI API calls per example. No explicit latency/dollar numbers reported. Forward-looking + confidence gating is the efficiency lever (retrieve only when uncertain).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k per dataset capped by the LM context window: top-2 documents for 2WikiMultihopQA, top-3 for StrategyQA, top-3 for ASQA/ASQA-hint, top-5 for WikiAsp (max that fits within text-davinci-003's input length limit). Only the current step's retrieved documents are kept (previous retrieved documents discarded each step) to stay within the context budget. Trigger threshold theta and masking threshold beta are dataset-specific (e.g., 2WikiMultihopQA theta=0.8, beta=0.4, implicit; StrategyQA theta=0.4; ASQA/WikiAsp theta=0.8, explicit).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (method paper, not a survey). It does, however, present a generalized framework of active retrieval (when and what to retrieve) and re-casts prior multi-time methods within it.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks; does not construct a new dataset). Evaluation subsets: 2WikiMultihopQA 500, StrategyQA 229, ASQA 500, WikiAsp 500 examples.
builds_on: Single-time RAG (Lewis et al. 2020 RAG, REALM Guu et al. 2020, REPLUG Shi et al. 2023, Atlas Izacard et al. 2022); fixed-interval/passive multi-time retrieval (KNN-LM Khandelwal et al. 2020, RETRO Borgeaud et al. 2022, IC-RALM Ram et al. 2023); interleaved CoT retrieval IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022); question-decomposition self-ask (Press et al. 2022); generated-query/hypothetical-document retrieval (HyDE Gao et al. 2022, GAR Mao et al. 2021, recitation Sun et al. 2022, GenRead Yu et al. 2022); Toolformer (Schick et al. 2023, inspires FLARE-instruct); LM calibration (Jiang et al. 2021, Kadavath et al. 2022). Base LM GPT-3.5 text-davinci-003 (Ouyang et al. 2022) and gpt-3.5-turbo; BM25 (Robertson & Zaragoza 2009); DPR Wikipedia dump (Karpukhin et al. 2020).
contrasts_with: Passive fixed-interval multi-time retrieval (KNN-LM, RETRO, IC-RALM -- previous-window) which may retrieve at inappropriate points; previous-sentence retrieval (IRCoT) which uses past context not reflecting future intent; question-decomposition (self-ask) which needs task-specific manual sub-question annotation limiting generalizability; single-time retrieve-and-generate which retrieves only once on the input. FLARE's distinctions: (1) retrieve only when the LM is uncertain (token-confidence trigger), and (2) query with the forward-looking anticipated next sentence rather than past context, with no task-specific annotation.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving) -- active/adaptive retrieval-augmented generation. A foundational token-confidence-triggered, forward-looking active RAG method for long-form generation; sits between fixed-schedule iterative RAG (IRCoT, IC-RALM) and later adaptive/self-reflective RAG (e.g., Self-RAG, Adaptive-RAG), pioneering the 'retrieve only when uncertain, query with anticipated content' pattern.
